text: Sixteen lessons ago, Support had one working report, and Finance had a question the data couldn't answer. This lesson closes out everything built since then.

Real semi-structured ingestion: the ticketing API's JSON, landed in a VARIANT column, parsed with real colon syntax. A Stream tracking exactly what changed, no watermark column. Two Tasks, each gated on SYSTEM dollar STREAM HAS DATA, each doing a genuinely different job: an idempotent upsert for Support's current state, an append-only log for Finance's events. Two views, two real Power BI pages, both built on that one shared foundation.

The part that mattered most in Lessons 13 through 15 wasn't MERGE syntax or a function signature. It was a transferable habit: reproduce the symptom exactly, isolate the pattern, confirm a hypothesis with a real tool before changing anything, fix the root cause instead of patching the damage. That duplicate Task is the exact kind of thing that happens the first time someone touches a working pipeline for real.

The existing Advanced capstone builds this same company's full production pipeline — dbt, Airflow, Terraform, CI/CD, the RBAC and masking this chapter's own Power BI connection relied on. This chapter stayed narrower on purpose: Streams and Tasks, in real depth, without that broader tooling competing for attention.

If you haven't built the Advanced capstone, it's the natural next step, same company, same conventions. If you have, revisit its own Streams and Tasks lessons with this chapter's bug fresh in mind — the same overlapping-execution risk applies anywhere a Stream has more than one consumer.
